title: Grateful Dead Live at Carthay Studios on 1966-03-19

ai_review.summary: Clean sound‑board recording of the historic March 19 1966 Pico Acid Test with standout early blues cuts like Heads Up and Midnight Hour, though the performance is more historically interesting than musically spectacular.
ai_review.review: This SBD capture offers a surprisingly clear and stereo‑rich listen for a 1966 audience tape, preserving Jerry Garcia’s high‑in‑the‑mix guitar work on early blues numbers such as Heads Up and The Midnight Hour.  While reviewers note the set is mostly raw R&B material with occasional off‑key vocals from Bob Weir, the historical value of hearing one of the earliest documented shows outweighs any musical imperfections.

ai_rating.rationale: Ten detailed reviews provide a balanced view: many praise the recording’s fidelity and historic significance, while others criticize identification issues and modest musical depth.  Weighted toward show quality (70%) and recording quality (30%), the overall score lands just under four stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Several reviewers call it ‘magnificent’, ‘clean and upfront’, and note excellent stereo separation.  One mentions a slight loss of fidelity compared to other ’66 tapes, and another suggests the mix is a bit Jerry‑heavy and may benefit from mono conversion.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A brief, early‑Dead blues set typical of the Pico Acid Test – raw R&B arrangements with limited improvisation, valuable more for its historical snapshot than for polished performance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar is high in the mix and praised as blistering blues work on Heads Up, Stormy Monday Jam, and Midnight Hour.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal is noted as slightly off‑key on several tracks.
